_comment: Single source of truth for spark types. `participant` is the plain-language phrasing shown in the Mark-moment popover; `label` and `definition` are for researchers and the LLM detector.

types.label: Additive
types.participant: This brought up something I hadn't considered
types.definition: New information, option, stakeholder, consequence, tool or resource enters the participant's search space.
types.cues: Participant picks up a fact/option/library/stakeholder they did not mention before and starts using it.
types.example_dilemma: AI points out a stakeholder the participant's initial essay ignored; the final essay weighs that stakeholder.
types.example_agentic: Agent uses a library the mathematician didn't know existed; they adopt it.

types.label: Representational
types.participant: This changed how I see the problem
types.definition: A new conceptualisation or framing of the problem: what kind of problem it is, what matters, what the goal is.
types.cues: Participant restates the problem in new terms, changes the end goal, or adopts a new organising frame.
types.example_dilemma: Participant stops treating it as honesty-vs-kindness and reframes it as a question about autonomy.
types.example_agentic: Trader reframes 'pick winning stocks' as 'manage exposure to one macro factor'.

types.label: Reflective
types.participant: Putting it into words, I realised something
types.definition: The act of explaining, answering or articulating (often prompted by the AI) leads the participant to an insight drawn from their own knowledge.
types.cues: Insight appears inside the participant's OWN message, often after being asked to explain or justify. The trigger may be an AI question.
types.example_dilemma: Asked why fairness matters here, the participant realises their view rests on a personal experience.
types.example_agentic: While describing their edge to the agent, a trader realises their real edge is industry knowledge, not timing.

types.label: Contrastive
types.participant: Disagreeing with it made my own view clearer
types.definition: Rejecting or pushing back on the AI's proposal clarifies or sharpens the participant's own beliefs or requirements.
types.cues: Participant disagrees, then articulates a sharper position or constraint than they had before.
types.example_dilemma: AI argues for strict impartiality; participant rejects it and articulates a clear account of special obligations.
types.example_agentic: Agent proposes a momentum strategy; trader rejects it and states their risk constraints precisely for the first time.

types.label: Counterfactual
types.definition: A hypothetical variation (what if X weren't true / were different) changes how the participant reasons about the actual case.
types.cues: 'What if', 'suppose', 'imagine if' exchanges followed by a changed or more nuanced position.
types.example_dilemma: 'What if the promise had been made under pressure?' leads the participant to a conditional view.
types.example_agentic: 'What if rates stay flat?' leads the trader to add a hedge.

types.label: Associative
types.participant: This connected to something I already knew
types.definition: Linking two ideas the participant already knew but had not connected, or connecting to past experience.
types.cues: 'This is like...', 'reminds me of...', participant brings in an analogy or prior experience that reorganises their thinking.
types.example_dilemma: Participant links the dilemma to a workplace whistleblowing situation they lived through.
types.example_agentic: Gamer links a game studio's engagement metrics to its revenue guidance.

types.label: Generative error
types.participant: Its mistake pointed me somewhere useful
types.definition: An incorrect, failed or partial AI output that nonetheless leads the participant to a productive idea.
types.cues: AI output is wrong or fails (error, wrong claim, bad code) but the participant extracts something useful from it.
types.example_dilemma: AI misstates a legal fact; checking it leads the participant to a relevant consideration.
types.example_agentic: Agent's proof attempt fails but uses a library that becomes the next step.

uptake.participant: I built on it with my own reasoning
I mostly went along with its view
I used its wording or answer directly
In the end it didn't change anything
